subject: generating a draw from a halfnormal

messages.author: b7954cd5c804c370
messages.subject: generating a draw from a halfnormal
parts:
Hi Stan users,

I'm trying to do posterior predictive checks, and running into an issue where a generated value should be positive but isn't.

In my model I fit a bunch of beta parameters, which are constrained to be positive. The betas are ~ halfnormal(mu, sigma), where mu and sigma are both positive halfnormal(0, 1).

However, when I run it with a generated quantities block drawing gen_beta ~ normal(mu, sigma), I get negative beta values. For example, on one chain I got this error, but on others I've just had clear evidence that it generated negative values:

[1] "Error : model15bab48673c_model3_namespace::write_array: gen_beta[k0__][9] is -0.261292, but must be greater than or equal to 0"

In an earlier post in 2013 ("Sampling from a half normal") Ben suggests that this ought to work, but perhaps something has changed. FWIW I'm using a devtools installed version of 2.8.0 from ~Sep 18, through rstan. 

Relevant parts of my model file:

parameters {
    vector<lower=0>[J] beta[2];
    vector<lower=0>[2] mu;
    vector<lower=0>[2] sigma;
}
model {
    //stuff that doesn't matter

    beta[1] ~ normal(mu[1], sigma[1]);
    beta[2] ~ normal(mu[2], sigma[2]);
    mu ~ normal(0, 1);
    sigma ~ normal(0, 1);
}
generated quantities {
    vector<lower=0>[J] gen_beta[2];

        gen_beta[1][d] <- normal_rng(mu[1], sigma[1]);
        gen_beta[2][d] <- normal_rng(mu[2], sigma[2]);
}

And here are the fitted mu and sigma values:
mu[1]         0.09     0.0  0.02    0.06    0.08    0.09    0.10    0.12   258 1.01
mu[2]         0.26     0.0  0.03    0.20    0.23    0.26    0.28    0.32   370 1.00
sigma[1]      0.02     0.0  0.01    0.01    0.01    0.02    0.03    0.05   142 1.02
sigma[2]      0.08     0.0  0.03    0.02    0.05    0.07    0.10    0.15   177 1.02


Thanks for any guidance,
Chris

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] generating a draw from a halfnormal
parts:
Good point. We don't have truncated random number generators.

There are two alternatives that occur to me.

1. Do your own rejection sampling in generated quantities.

a <- -1;
while (a < 0)
a <- normal_rng(mu, sigma);

It should be OK in terms of speed as long as (mu + sigma) > 0
(acceptance rate will be > 1/3 that way). So in your case,
as long as you init in a reasonable place for mu and sigma, you
should be OK.

2. A more general solution is to move the generated quantity
variable to parameters and put the lower bound on it and
then replace the RNGs with sampling statements.

parameters {
...

vector<lower=0>[J] gen_beta[2];
gen_beta[1][d] <- normal_rng(mu[1], sigma[1]);
gen_beta[2][d] <- normal_rng(mu[2], sigma[2]);

model {
...
gen_beta[1] ~ normal(mu[1], sigma[1]);
gen_beta[2] ~ normal(mu[2], sigma[2]);


I vectorized your generated quantities --- I think there's
a missing (d in 1:J) there because you're not defining
all of gen_beta.

- Bob
